subject: maths
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF

topics.title: Position words: top-bottom, inside-outside, near-far
outcomes: Learner can describe where an object is using position words (upar-neeche, andar-bahar, paas-door) in English and the home language
misconceptions: Believes left and right are fixed places in the room rather than relative to the person facing
hooks: Find the cat hiding under the charpai or behind the matka at home

topics.title: Comparing: big-small, more-less, tall-short
outcomes: Learner can compare two collections or objects and say which has more, fewer, or the same
misconceptions: Thinks a row of objects spread out has more objects than the same number bunched together
hooks: Two plates of laddoos: which plate has more? spread one plate out and ask again

topics.title: Sorting and matching
outcomes: Learner can sort objects by one attribute (colour, size, shape) and explain the rule used
misconceptions: Thinks objects can be sorted only by colour
hooks: Sort a mixed handful of rajma, chana and moong

chapters.title: What is Long? What is Round?

topics.title: Long and round things
outcomes: Learner can identify objects around them as long or round and explain their choice
misconceptions: Thinks a shape changes its name when it is turned or moved
hooks: Bangles, rotis and wheels are round; pencils and sugarcane are long

topics.title: Things that roll, slide or stack
outcomes: Learner can predict and check whether an object will roll, slide or stack
misconceptions: Believes only balls can roll
hooks: Roll a bottle, a ladoo and a matchbox down a slanted notebook

topics.title: Counting objects up to 9
outcomes: Learner can count up to 9 objects by touching each one once and say the last number as the total
misconceptions: Counts some objects twice or skips some (one-to-one correspondence error)
Thinks the last number said is just the name of the last object, not how many there are
hooks: Count mangoes in the basket while sharing them with cousins

topics.title: Reading and writing numerals 1 to 9 (and zero)
outcomes: Learner can match a numeral and its number name to a collection of that size
misconceptions: Writes 6 and 9 or 2 and 5 mirror-wise and thinks it does not matter
Believes zero means nothing is there so it is not a number
hooks: Bus numbers and house numbers on the street

topics.title: Comparing and ordering numbers to 9
outcomes: Learner can say which of two numbers is more or less and place numbers 1 to 9 in order
misconceptions: Thinks bigger-looking objects make a bigger number
hooks: Who has more mangoes: 7 small ones or 4 big ones?

topics.title: Making 10 in different ways
outcomes: Learner can show pairs of numbers that make 10 using fingers, beads or objects
misconceptions: Believes there is only one way to make 10 (like 5 and 5)
hooks: Ten fingers: fold some, how many are still up?

topics.title: Numbers 11 to 20 as ten and some more
outcomes: Learner can represent numbers 11 to 20 as one ten and some ones
misconceptions: Writes fourteen as 41 because the "four" is heard first in the word
Thinks 1 in 15 means just one, not one ten
hooks: Bundles of 10 ice-cream sticks plus loose sticks

chapters.title: How Many?
chapters.theme: Addition and Subtraction of Single Digit Numbers

topics.title: Putting together (addition within 9)
outcomes: Learner can solve simple "putting together" stories by counting on and write them as a + b = c
misconceptions: Thinks the = sign means "write the answer here" rather than "is the same as"
Always counts all from 1 instead of counting on from the larger number
hooks: 3 parrots on a guava tree, 2 more come

topics.title: Taking away (subtraction within 9)
outcomes: Learner can solve "taking away" and "how many more" stories using objects or a number line
misconceptions: Believes subtraction can be done in any order, like 3 - 5 = 2
hooks: 5 rotis on the plate, brother eats 2

topics.title: Adding up to 20 using "make 10"
outcomes: Learner can add numbers with sums up to 20 by first making 10
misconceptions: Thinks adding always means counting every object from 1
hooks: 8 tomatoes and 5 tomatoes: move 2 to fill the 10-crate

topics.title: Subtracting within 20
outcomes: Learner can subtract within 20 by counting back or thinking of the related addition
misconceptions: Subtracts the smaller digit from the bigger one in 13 - 5 and gets 12
hooks: Sabziwala sold 6 of his 15 brinjals

topics.title: Longer-shorter, taller-shorter
outcomes: Learner can compare lengths of two objects by placing them side by side from the same starting point
misconceptions: Thinks the object that sticks out further is longer even when the ends are not lined up
hooks: Who is tallest in the family photo: dadi, papa or Lina?

topics.title: Measuring with hand-spans and footsteps
outcomes: Learner can measure lengths using non-standard units like hand-spans, footsteps or pencils and count the units
misconceptions: Believes the number of hand-spans will be the same no matter whose hand is used
hooks: Measure the dining mat with your bitta and then with papa’s

topics.title: Heavier and lighter
outcomes: Learner can compare the weight of two objects by lifting or using a simple balance
misconceptions: Thinks the bigger object is always heavier
hooks: A big pillow vs a small stone

topics.title: Counting in tens and ones up to 99
outcomes: Learner can group objects in tens and ones and write the number they make up to 99
misconceptions: Writes forty-six as 406 (writes the tens as 40 then the 6)
hooks: Bundles of 10 bangles on the bangle-seller’s rod

topics.title: Number names and patterns on a number grid
outcomes: Learner can read and write numbers to 99 and spot patterns in a 1–100 number grid
misconceptions: Thinks 29 comes before 20 because it has a 9 in it
hooks: Snakes and ladders board numbers

topics.title: Repeating patterns
outcomes: Learner can identify the repeating unit in a pattern and extend it
misconceptions: Thinks a pattern must use only colours, not shapes, sounds or actions
hooks: Diya-rangoli-diya-rangoli during Diwali; clap-snap rhythms

topics.title: Making own patterns
outcomes: Learner can create a repeating pattern and describe its rule to a friend
misconceptions: Believes any random arrangement is a pattern
hooks: String a mala with two colours of beads

chapters.title: How do I Spend my Day?

topics.title: Sequencing daily events
outcomes: Learner can order daily activities using words like before, after, morning, afternoon, evening, night
misconceptions: Thinks "yesterday" and "tomorrow" mean the same thing
hooks: Brush, nashta, school, play, dinner: what comes first?

topics.title: Which takes longer?
outcomes: Learner can compare two activities and say which takes more time
misconceptions: Believes an activity that is more fun takes less time
hooks: Eating a banana vs walking to school

topics.title: Equal groups and repeated addition
outcomes: Learner can count objects arranged in equal groups by adding the same number again and again
misconceptions: Counts groups instead of objects when asked how many in all
hooks: 3 auto-rickshaws with 3 wheels each: how many wheels?

topics.title: Counting in twos and fives
outcomes: Learner can count things that come in pairs or fives by saying every second or fifth number
misconceptions: Thinks 2 + 2 + 2 and "three twos" give different answers
hooks: Pairs of chappals outside the temple; fingers on hands

topics.title: Recognising coins and notes
outcomes: Learner can recognise coins and notes of common values and make small amounts
misconceptions: Thinks more coins always means more money
Believes a bigger-sized coin always has more value
hooks: Play kirana shop with ₹1, ₹2, ₹5 and ₹10 coins

topics.title: Buying within a budget
outcomes: Learner can decide what can be bought with a given small amount
misconceptions: Thinks the money left over is lost
hooks: ₹10 at the mela: a balloon for ₹5 and what else?

topics.title: Sorting and counting to answer a question
outcomes: Learner can sort objects, count each group and answer "which is most / least?"
misconceptions: Thinks the group that takes up more space has more items
hooks: Count toys by type in the class toy box

topics.title: Showing counts with pictures
outcomes: Learner can show counts by drawing or stacking one picture or block per item and compare the rows
misconceptions: Compares rows by how long they look even when pictures are drawn different sizes
hooks: Stack blocks to show how many cars, dolls and balls
